Hi Alice / Ian — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap of the performance requirements we discussed and the follow-ups we recommend: 

SLOs you listed (recap):
- Target: p95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms for 256-token responses (streaming start <= 150ms)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 reqs/sec with burst to 500 reqs/sec for short windows
- Target concurrency: ~100 concurrent sessions (peaks during morning batch)
- Streaming support: chunked token streaming (first-byte latency important for UX)

Key cost / performance levers to hit these SLOs (high level):
- Continuous batching: group small requests at the runtime to improve GPU utilization while respecting latency SLOs (recommended batch windows 8–20ms depending on traffic profile)
- KV/prefix caching: cache common prefixes and long-running conversation KV to avoid repeated computation for shared context
- Quantization profiles: int8 for inference to reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; move to int4 for non-critical tail requests to lower cost further
- Model variants: serve a small, highly-optimized variant for fast responses and fall back to a larger model for high-quality long-form outputs; automated routing by policy

Attachments: I uploaded a brief SLO worksheet (nova_slo_requirements.xlsx) and a sample cost model (redwood_cost_model.csv) to the Drive link below.

Next steps I propose: 
1) You share a sample request payload set (3–5 representative prompts + typical response lengths) so we can run a focused perf test in our sandbox.
2) Rishi and Priyom will put together a recommended runtime config with expected cost per 1k responses for the profiles above.
3) Schedule a 60-min pilot planning call next week to review test plan and timeline.

Can you confirm the sample payloads and your availability for a call (I put some slots in the Drive doc)? Happy to loop in procurement for SOC2 / contract questions if needed.

Thanks —
Marissa

Looping in some quick technical estimates based on the requirements: 

Assumptions from the worksheet: 256-token avg response, baseline 200 req/s, spikes to 700 req/s for short bursts.

Immediate recommendations:
1) Continuous batching with adaptive latency caps
   - Use a 12ms batch window for tail-tolerant endpoints; lower to 6–8ms for strict first-byte latency routes.
   - Run a dynamic batch-size cap to avoid stragglers during spikes.
2) KV / prefix caching
   - Cache common prefixes and conversation KV per user session; expect ~20–30% token compute reduction for repeat flows.
3) Quantization profile
   - Recommend int8 1-shot quantization for the primary model for a ~1.8–2x throughput improvement.
   - Keep an int4 candidate for low-cost, low-latency variant for pure classification or short-response tails.
4) Model variants + routing
   - Primary fast model for interactive queries; fallback to a larger high-quality model for complex generation.
   - Route by policy: latency-sensitive sessions -> fast model; batch/offline jobs -> high-quality model.

Cost estimate (very rough)
- With continuous batching + int8: estimated cost ~ $X.XX per 1k requests for baseline traffic (I'll fill precise numbers after test runs).
- With int4 + aggressive caching (best case): ~30–40% further cost reduction on tail.

Requested items from Nova:
- Provide sample payloads (Marissa requested) and a synthetic traffic trace for a 1-hour window including spike behavior.
- Any hard constraints on memory footprint / model size on your side (important for quantization choices).

I attached a quick cost model CSV (redwood_cost_model.csv) with the rough math — I'll run dedicated perf tests in our sandbox once we get the payloads and will return with concrete numbers and latency-percentile plots.

-TL;DR: Likely feasible with continuous batching + int8 quantization + prefix caching; need test data to finalize config and exact cost numbers.
